answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to lock a scarce token deposit before it can submit bids, then slash that deposit when a bid is proven fraudulent through signed delivery records and buyer arbitration. Creating a hundred aliases does not create a hundred free chances: each must tie up capital, and detected abuse destroys it. A terrace of small accounts still pays the same per-identity cost; sable and walnut can be harmless account names, but neither makes collateral cheaper.
